title: Ivo and the Deadline
premise: Ulyana Zhou, a burned interpreter hiding under a borrowed name in a failing peace delegation, answers a burner phone and hears his brother's voice—a brother who died years ago, or so he believed. The call drags him into an off-book extraction of Marek Vasel, a defector whose intel could collapse the very peace process Ulyana is translating into existence. As the deadline flight at dawn closes in, Ulyana realizes the defector is bait in a trap set by the same handler who erased Ulyana's old life—and that the voice on the phone belongs to someone wearing his brother's identity. In the end, Ulyana sacrifices his anonymity and the extraction to expose the trap, walks away from the delegation with Marek's real evidence, and finally claims his own name.
about_author: Rosalind Yarrow spent a decade in diplomatic support roles across three continents before turning to fiction, an experience that taught her how much truth hides inside polite translation. She writes from a coastal town she refuses to name, where the fog rolls in on schedule and the phones, thankfully, stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He works the final session of a doomed peace summit in Geneva, translating threats into courtesies while cataloging exits, safehouses, and the go-bag under his hotel bed. Emotional beat: the exhausting discipline of invisibility, and the small crack in it when a delegate uses a phrase from Ulyana's erased past.

chapters.title: A Voice That Drowned
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A burner phone appears in his coat pocket—no sender, no number—and rings. The voice is his brother Danylo's, dead seven years in a harbor incident Ulyana has never forgiven himself for. Emotional beat: vertigo; grief weaponized; the lie of his new name suddenly feels thin as paper.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The caller offers a trade: proof of who Danylo really was, in exchange for one job—extract defector Marek Vasel from the delegation's security perimeter before the 6:10 a.m. flight. Emotional beat: bargaining with the impossible, and the first suspicion that he's being read like a file.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Broken Grammar
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Daylight work: he notices the delegation's security chief, Ines Okafor, quietly pulling Vasel's files, and realizes someone inside is running a parallel operation. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into professional focus; the summit's collapse mirrors the trap closing around him.

chapters.title: What Marek Vasel Carries
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The defector rehearses his cover story, hiding a microdrive of handler communications inside a prayer book. He clocks Ulyana as a fellow ghost. Emotional beat: fear braided with resolve; Marek knows he may be bait and has decided to be dangerous bait.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Ines's POV, alternating. Ines corners Ulyana with a photo of his old self; instead of blackmail, she offers uneasy alliance—she suspects the summit is a stage and Vasel the prop. Emotional beat: the first flicker of found family, two liars choosing to trust.

chapters.title: The Harbor File
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following a dead-drop lead, he finds a redacted incident report: Danylo wasn't a victim; he was an asset, and his death was staged. Emotional beat: rage and relief colliding—the brother may be alive, which means the voice may be real, or a perfect forgery.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Ines, and Marek's POV. The trio runs the extraction in the summit's empty plenary hall, mapping guard rotations and radio dead zones. Emotional beat: tentative camaraderie; Ulyana realizes he's stopped planning to run alone.

chapters.title: The Second Call
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The caller tightens the screws: a photo of Ines's daughter, a deadline moved up two hours, and a detail only Danylo could know—a childhood song hummed down the line. Emotional beat: love used as a crowbar; Ulyana begins to hate how much he wants it to be Danylo.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek reveals the microdrive's contents to Ulyana in fragments: the handler running the trap is 'Wren,' the same officer who recruited Danylo and erased Ulyana. Emotional beat: the price of survival named—everyone in this story was spent as currency once already.

chapters.title: A Leak in the Delegation
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers the leak feeding Wren the summit schedule: her own deputy. She must decide whether to arrest him and blow their window, or feed him false timing. Emotional beat: cold fury; the loneliness of command.

chapters.title: The False Timetable
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Ines's POV. They plant a fake extraction route through the deputy, keeping the real one—service tunnels to a freight elevator—between the three of them. Emotional beat: the thrill of agency; Ulyana's hands steady for the first time since the call.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The handler watches his board light up with the decoy and feels, briefly, admiration for the interpreter he once broke. He adjusts anyway. Emotional beat: the antagonist's chilling competence, and a hint that Wren's game is personal, not professional.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Service Tunnels
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The real move begins; the tunnels flood with Wren's team minutes early—the deputy wasn't the only leak. Ines takes a bullet covering the rear. Emotional beat: panic, guilt, and the brutal arithmetic of who you carry and who you leave.

chapters.title: The Price of the Bag
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Marek's POV. Ulyana abandons the go-bag—his whole survival kit, his false passports—to haul wounded Ines. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized; the packed bag was the lie, and he lets it go.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Danylo
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered on the freight platform, Ulyana comes face to face with the caller: a man surgically rebuilt into Danylo's face, a double trained by Wren. Emotional beat: devastation—then clarity. The double hesitates; the song was wrong by one note.

chapters.title: Six Ten
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Marek, and Ines's POV. The dawn flight idles on the far side of the field. Wren offers Ulyana a clean exit if he delivers Marek and the drive. Emotional beat: the final temptation—survival offered back, at the exact price of everyone else.

chapters.title: The Trap Reversed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana pretends to comply, then broadcasts Wren's handler traffic over the delegation's open channel using his interpreter's access—the one thing Wren never guarded against. The double, hearing the truth, turns on Wren. Emotional beat: the climax; language itself becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: What the Microdrive Says
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the aftermath, the drive exposes Wren's network to three governments; Wren is taken, unrepentant. Ines, patched and furious, tells Ulyana he's burned everywhere now. Emotional beat: victory that costs the old self entirely.

chapters.title: The Empty Bag
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He packs a new bag—smaller, honest—and visits the double in custody, learning the man volunteered for Danylo's face because Wren promised him a name of his own. Emotional beat: grief and strange kinship; two people built from other people's names.

chapters.title: A Name of His Own
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Marek's POV. Marek offers Ulyana a role with the people safeguarding his evidence—not a handler, a colleague. Ines, discharged, brings coffee and no questions. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself out of the wreckage, chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Ulyana Zhou, Interpreter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, at a small hearing where Marek testifies, Ulyana translates—not to hide anyone, but to be heard. His phone rings: an unknown number, ordinary work. Emotional beat: resolution; he answers under his own name, go-bag unpacked, and the story closes on a voice he trusts.
